correctness.rationale: For every nonnegative gap triple, all factors with 0, 1 or 2 marked ones are exhaustively classified by borders. The exact maximizing-interval counts follow, including n=2. Counting disjoint parameter cases produces the four rational generating functions and coefficient identities. Lattice spacing convergence to Dirichlet(1,1,1) and explicit inclusion-exclusion simplex areas give the joint CDF and limiting expectations. Packaged KMP enumeration checked 16,215 literal words through n=46; an independent family and coefficient census checked n=2..180. These experiments corroborate but do not substitute for the proof.

IID asymptotics are not preserved under exponentially rare fixed-weight conditioning. The weight-three length theorem does not subsume a weight-two joint occurrence-count theorem.

originality.rationale: The exact “two-marker longest-border” result already implies the length marginal after identifying the least period; that marginal is explicitly excluded from the original contribution. What remains is a complete occurrence-interval multiplicity classification (one through four), a four-valued rational all-length enumerator with a unique extremizer at every eligible length, and a joint sparse-source length/multiplicity law. The closest publicly searchable records and materially read primary texts do not imply the new output multiplicity results; full texts of the closest indexed scientific records have now been inspected, with possible unindexed equivalence remaining the priority risk.

value.rationale: The motivating new 2026 algorithm reports ALL longest unbordered factor occurrences rather than only their length; exact interval output multiplicities are therefore a natural invariant. The theorem determines all four possible multiplicities for every sparse binary weight-two instance, supplies an all-length rational enumerator, proves the unique four-occurrence family, and gives the joint limit conditional on the two dominant multiplicities. The quantified occurrence output-size law is not a textbook length/period restatement and its full distribution is relevant to analyses of reporting algorithms on sparse strings.
